subject: Following up: model fit & benchmark links for Acme (post-demo)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Murphy <jake@acme.com>, Emma Li <emma@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick recap + recommended model choices and next steps

Jake / Emma — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

- Goals: 1) accurate entity extraction and high-recall classification for support tickets (~1k qps peak? you estimated 800 qps during product launches); 2) tight latency SLO for the customer-facing autocomplete (target p95 < 350ms at 512 tokens).
- Data: you said you can share a 1k-sample prompt set and a CSV of customer-ID mappings (thanks in advance).
- Recommended starting models (based on your latency and quality targets):
  • redwood-1.3b (low latency, good for interactive autocomplete)
  • redwood-7b-quant (best balance of quality/cost for classification + entity extraction)
  • redwood-14b (highest quality fallback for high-stakes routing/triage)

Benchmarks & what I’m sharing:
- Redwood-verified performance profile for the recommended models (TPS observed, p50/p95 latency at 128/512 tokens) — link below.
- Prompt set and suggested evaluation script (we'll run your 1k samples through our harness and provide per-intent recall/precision).

Attachments: acme-mappings.csv (your mapping stub), and I’ll attach a short PDF with our benchmark summary once the run completes.

Next steps:
1) Please drop the 1k sample prompts and a representative CSV in the Drive link I shared (or reply here).
2) I’ll kick off an initial model-fit benchmark and share the Redwood-verified profile (ETA 48 hours).
3) Marissa will propose a mutual action plan and pricing for a Dedicated slot if you'd like predictable throughput.

If the p95 numbers are the main gating factor, we can explore: smaller model for autocomplete + an asymmetric routing rule that sends complex classification calls to 7b-quant.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood-verified quick snapshot (from internal atlas): 
- redwood-1.3b: sustain ~60 TPS, p50=48ms @128 tokens / p95=120ms @512 tokens
- redwood-7b-quant: sustain ~28 TPS, p50=160ms @256 tokens / p95=420ms @512 tokens
- redwood-14b: sustain ~12 TPS, p50=240ms @256 tokens / p95=620ms @512 tokens

Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-model-fit-2026

From: Jake Murphy <jake@acme.com>

Alex — thanks for the quick follow-up and the numbers. A couple quick clarifying q's: 

1) For the p95 numbers you listed, are those with batching enabled and running on your Hosted API or on Dedicated hardware? We care about the worst-case interactive latency (no batching if possible).
2) Can you give a rough cost delta between redwood-1.3b and 7b-quant for our workload assumptions (we're mostly classification/NER, average response length ~220 tokens)?

Also attaching the sample CSV we discussed (small subset). We'll upload the 1k prompts today.

— Jake
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700

Marissa / Dylan — forwarding Jake's reply and the sample CSV. Can you do two things: 

- Marissa: please run the 1k prompt set through our evaluation harness (use the repo: /bench/evals/acme-2026) and publish the Redwood-verified performance profile (include TPS, p50/p95 at 128/256/512 tokens). Add the Drive and HubSpot links to the report. Target: EOD Wednesday PDT.
- Dylan: can you run a short Dedicated-equivalent stress test on a 7b-quant config and confirm p95 numbers with batching disabled (interactive mode)? We want to validate the "no-batching" interactive p95 for the UI flow Jake cares about. If you need a temp quota bump, let me know.

I’ve attached the sample CSV (acme-mappings.csv) that Jake sent. I’ll loop you both into the external thread after you have the initial report.

Thanks — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Murphy <jake@acme.com>, Emma Li <emma@acme.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + recommended model choices and next steps

Jake / Emma — thanks for the sample CSV and for the call. We completed the initial run and attached the Redwood-verified performance profile PDF (redwood-benchmark-acme.pdf). Summary highlights below: 

- Test setup: hosted Dedicated-equivalent vCPU/GPU profile, interactive mode (batching disabled), synthetic load to measure tail latency at per-request arrival pattern matching your spike windows.
- Key numbers (512-token context unless noted):
  • redwood-1.3b — sustained interactive throughput: ~58 TPS; p50=52ms; p95=135ms
  • redwood-7b-quant — sustained interactive throughput: ~30 TPS; p50=170ms; p95=410ms
  • redwood-14b — sustained interactive throughput: ~13 TPS; p50=250ms; p95=610ms

Notes & recommendations:
- For your autocomplete UI (p95 < 350ms), redwood-1.3b meets the SLO comfortably at typical payloads. For classification/NER quality, redwood-7b-quant shows materially better recall on our eval set (delta +6pp recall) and is our recommendation for the backend pipeline.
- Suggested architecture: use redwood-1.3b for low-latency interactive calls (autocomplete) and route classification/NER to 7b-quant asynchronously or via a fast fallback decision that can tolerate ~400ms p95.
- If you want a single-model solution, we can profile a 7b-quant Dedicated slot with autoscale headroom to ensure p95 < 350ms at your expected peak — Marissa can send an estimated commit for that.

Attached: redwood-benchmark-acme.pdf (full breakdown, per-intent precision/recall, boxplots of latency distribution), and the Drive link with the prompt set and run logs: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D5E

Next steps: 
- Jake: confirm whether you want us to produce a mutual action plan for a mixed-routing approach or a single Dedicated 7b-quant slot.
- Alex: I’ll prepare an ops doc with the routing rule examples and a quick canary plan.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
